s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdomen with chronic symptoms and weight loss, complicated by prior bariatric surgery
salient_findings: Localized tenderness and rebound pain in the right lower abdomen
Free gas under the right diaphragm on plain abdominal radiography
Thickened intestinal wall on abdominal CT
key_facts: One month history of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting
Weight loss of 23 kg due to poor appetite and abdominal pain
Sound of gas passing through water heard on physical examination

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdomen with chronic symptoms and weight loss, complicated by prior bariatric surgery
salient_findings: Localized tenderness and rebound pain in the right lower abdomen
Free gas under the right diaphragm on plain abdominal radiography
Thickened intestinal wall on abdominal CT
key_facts: One month history of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting

differentials: Kaposi sarcoma of the gastrointestinal tract
per_call: Kaposi sarcoma of the gastrointestinal tract

shortlist.label: Intestinal obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Mechanical obstruction suggested by abdominal radiography and CT findings, including dilated upper jejunum and 'spring sign'

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: History of prior bariatric surgery increases risk, and imaging findings of intestinal obstruction and pneumatosis are consistent with internal hernia

shortlist.label: Adhesional bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of bariatric surgery and weight loss, combined with imaging findings of intestinal obstruction, make adhesional bowel obstruction a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Marginal ulceration
shortlist.why_kept: Prior bariatric surgery increases risk of marginal ulceration, and patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and vomiting are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal fistula
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of pneumatosis and thickened intestinal wall, combined with patient's history of bariatric surgery, suggest possible gastrointestinal fistula

raw.rationale: The patient's history of bariatric surgery, symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, along with imaging findings of dilated upper jejunum with 'spring sign' and constriction of the junction of gastric fundus and body, are consistent with an internal hernia, a known complication of bariatric surgery.

rejected.label: Intestinal obstruction
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms and imaging findings consistent with obstruction, internal hernia is a more specific diagnosis that explains the patient's presentation and history.

rejected.label: Adhesional bowel obstruction
rejected.why: There is no clear history of previous abdominal surgery or other risk factors for adhesions, making internal hernia a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Marginal ulceration
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not specifically suggest marginal ulceration, and the presence of free gas under the diaphragm and scattered pneumatosis in the abdominal cavity are more consistent with an internal hernia.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal fistula
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not specifically suggest a gastrointestinal fistula, and the presence of dilated upper jejunum with 'spring sign' is more consistent with an internal hernia.

gold: Gastric band erosion with migration to jejunum causing intestinal obstruction and jejunal perforation
